about: a message that holds a failure and the decision it led to: the user types that the C extension crashed on one build and that they therefore dropped it; the agent's reply takes in the drop and says nothing more of the crash. Invented text. Before 1.5.1 the sorter labeled such a message a decision only, and when it labeled both, one of the two was lost (a source backed one event). The answers here were recorded from real Haiku (sort) and Sonnet (draft, review) calls with the 1.5.1 wording: both labeled, the failure and then the decision written, the decision with because set to the failure's place in the list.

sources.text: Before we go on: which build of the parser do the benchmarks use?
The benchmarks use the pure Python build. The speedups folder holds an optional C extension that the benchmark script imports only when it is installed.
The C extension crashed on the Windows build, so I dropped it. We stay pure Python.

Noted: pure Python, no C extension.

One thing to check: was the 2.1x measured with the C extension in the build or without it? If the benchmarked build still included the extension, or the old-vs-new gap came partly from it, the number may not hold for the pure Python parser. If both runs were pure Python, the result stands as is.

If the paper or README mentions the extension, those mentions should come out too. I can grep the repo and paper.tex for them if you would like.
Thanks, that is useful to know.
Understood. I will leave the Results text as it is until then.
Nothing else is pending from me.
